mainTopic: How often אבשלום cut his hair, and the source for a thirty-day סתם נזירות
overview: The amud continues a ברייתא about how often אבשלום, a נזיר, cut his hair. רבי says once every twelve months, learned by a גזירה שוה from the word ימים by בתי ערי חומה. רבי נהוראי says every thirty days, and רבי יוסי says every ערב שבת. The גמרא defends רבי's source against several challenges: other פסוקים where ימים means two years, thirty days, or appears as ימימה. It rules that a plain ימים must be learned from an identical plain ימים. It then explains רבי נהוראי's thirty days through the weight of the hair, and shows how רבי יוסי's weekly haircut still set אבשלום apart from his brothers. After a short note about the 'forty years' in the פסוק, a new משנה teaches that an unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days. רב מתנא learns this from the גימטריא of יהיה. בר פדא counts the word נזיר and gets twenty-nine, and the גמרא explains why רב מתנא does not use that count.

steps.title: רבי learns twelve months from walled-city houses
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns that the word ימים by אבשלום means twelve months, through a גזירה שוה from בתי ערי חומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי learns 'days' from 'days' in the passage about houses in walled cities. Just as there it means twelve months, so too here it means twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains where רבי gets his view that אבשלום cut his hair once a year. He links the word ימים in the פסוק about אבשלום to the same word in the passage about houses in walled cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ימים alone is unclear, since it could mean a few days or a longer stretch. By walled-city houses the תורה says right there that the time is a full year, so רבי carries that meaning over to אבשלום. This is the method called גזירה שוה: the same word in two places teaches the same meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Houses in walled cities, which can be bought back only within one year of their sale
Just as there... so too here. The standard way of comparing two cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה שוה is the base that the rest of this section challenges and defends.

phrases.english: And he derives "days" from "days"
phrases.notes: ימים appears in the פסוק about אבשלום (שמואל ב 14:26) and also in ויקרא 25:29 about walled-city houses.

phrases.english: from houses of walled cities.
Just as there it is twelve months,
phrases.notes: The very next פסוק there (ויקרא 25:30) says 'a full year.'

phrases.english: so too here it is twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section, giving the source for רבי's view of once every twelve months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ימים by אבשלום means twelve months, learned by גזירה שוה from בתי ערי חומה.

steps.title: Two other views: every thirty days or every Friday
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי says אבשלום cut his hair every thirty days. רבי יוסי says every ערב שבת, like princes do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: he cut his hair once every thirty days. רבי יוסי says: he cut it every Friday, for we find that the sons of kings cut their hair every Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings two other opinions on how often אבשלום cut his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נהוראי gives a much shorter time, thirty days. רבי יוסי gives an even shorter time, once a week, and his reason is royal custom: princes groomed themselves before שבת. So there are now three views: a year, a month, and a week.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we find. Introduces a supporting example

phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says:
He would cut his hair once every thirty days.
Rabbi Yosei says:
He would cut his hair from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve,
for so we find with the sons of kings
that they cut their hair from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלֵּחַ אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other opinions that disagree with רבי's twelve months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נהוראי: every thirty days. רבי יוסי: every ערב שבת, like princes.

steps.title: רבי elsewhere reads ימים there as two days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רבי's source and then challenges it: רבי himself says ימים by walled-city houses means at least two days, not a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's reason? He learns it from houses of walled cities. But isn't it רבי himself who said: 'days' means no fewer than two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first repeats רבי's source to set up its question. Then it attacks: רבי himself reads ימים by walled-city houses as two days, so how can he learn twelve months from there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה carries the meaning of a word from one place to another. In another place, רבי says the ימים by walled-city houses means 'at least two days.' If that is what the word means there, the גזירה שוה should give two days for אבשלום, not twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it... Opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that רבי made up a new reading. The same passage has two time words: 'a full year' and ימים. רבי reads the word ימים itself as two days, so the problem is which meaning the גזירה שוה should carry over.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?
He derives it from houses of walled cities.
But isn't it Rabbi who said:
"Days" means no fewer than two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי's גזירה שוה from step 1 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's גזירה שוה that ימים by אבשלום means twelve months.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי himself reads ימים by walled-city houses as two days, so the גזירה שוה should give two days, not twelve months.

steps.title: Two days cannot fit, because the hair must be heavy
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה was learned because of the hair's weight. Two days of growth adds no weight, so for אבשלום only the twelve-month meaning fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: This גזירה שוה was learned because of the weight, and in two days there is no weight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the פסוק says אבשלום cut his hair when it got heavy, a two-day meaning makes no sense for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק by אבשלום says he cut his hair because it was heavy on him. Hair does not get heavy in two days, so the 'two days' meaning cannot apply to him. The גזירה שוה therefore carries over the year-long meaning from the walled-city passage instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from the same word used in two places
Was learned / received as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's twelve months stands. The weight of אבשלום's hair rules out two days, so the year-long meaning of ימים is what the גזירה שוה brings over.

phrases.english: This verbal analogy
was learned because of the weight,
phrases.notes: The פסוק says אבשלום cut his hair because it was heavy on him (שמואל ב 14:26).

phrases.english: and in two days there is no weight.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מִשּׁוּם כּוֹבֶד גְּמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 and defends רבי's גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Context limits which meaning the גזירה שוה carries over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי reads ימים by walled-city houses as two days, the גזירה שוה should give two days for אבשלום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two days of growth adds no weight, which does not fit the פסוק about אבשלום, so the twelve-month meaning is the one applied to him.

steps.title: Maybe ימים means two years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ימים by אבשלום could mean two years, based on a פסוק about פרעה's dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say ימים means two years, since the תורה writes 'And it was at the end of two years of days'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we learn ימים from בתי ערי חומה. Another פסוק uses ימים together with two years, so maybe ימים means two years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said ימים by אבשלום means twelve months. The גמרא points to the פסוק before יוסף is called to פרעה, where ימים appears next to 'two years.' If that is the model, אבשלום would have cut his hair every two years.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, a way of offering another possibility
Two years of days, meaning two full years

phrases.english: But say it means two years,
as it is written: “And it was at the end of two years of days”?!
phrases.notes: בראשית 41:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now accepts that ימים means a longer period. It asks why the source must be בתי ערי חומה and not a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice of בתי ערי חומה as the source for ימים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק uses ימים to describe two years, so it could just as easily be the model.

steps.title: Learn plain ימים only from plain ימים
steps.stepSummary: ימים that stands alone is learned from another ימים that stands alone, not from one that comes with the word 'years.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn ימים that has no 'years' with it from another ימים that has no 'years' with it. This case, which has 'years' with it, cannot prove anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about two years does not fit. There, ימים comes together with the word 'years.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By אבשלום and by בתי ערי חומה, ימים stands alone. In פרעה's dream it is attached to שנתים, and that is where the 'two years' comes from. A plain ימים has to be compared to another plain ימים.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive one case from another
And let it not prove, meaning it is not a fair comparison
That has with it, meaning another word comes along with it

phrases.english: We learn “ימים” that has no “years” with it
phrases.notes: This is the ימים by אבשלום.

phrases.english: from “ימים” that has no “years” with it,
phrases.notes: This is the ימים by בתי ערי חומה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: and let this one, which has “years” with it, not prove anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the sources: the wording of the two פסוקים is not the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ימים in תנ"ך could be the source, including one that comes with 'two years.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a ימים that stands alone, like the one by בתי ערי חומה, can teach about the plain ימים by אבשלום.

steps.title: Maybe ימים means thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ימים could mean thirty days, from the פסוק about the meat in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say ימים means thirty days, since it is written 'until a month of days'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another פסוק. There, ימים is used for a month, so maybe אבשלום cut his hair every thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would match רבי נהוראי's view from step 2, that אבשלום cut his hair every thirty days. The challenge asks why רבי did not learn from this פסוק instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A month of days, a full month

phrases.english: But say it means thirty days,
as it is written: “Until a month of days”!
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proposed source, built the same way as step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice of בתי ערי חומה as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק uses ימים for thirty days, which would give a different meaning.

steps.title: Plain ימים is not learned from ימים with 'month'
steps.stepSummary: The same answer as before: the ימים in that פסוק comes with the word 'month,' so it cannot teach about a plain ימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn ימים that has no 'months' with it from another ימים that has no 'months' with it. This case, which has 'months' with it, cannot prove anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the thirty-day source for the same reason it rejected the two-year source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'עד חדש ימים' the thirty days come from the word חדש, not from ימים. Since the ימים by אבשלום stands alone, it must be compared to the ימים by בתי ערי חומה, which also stands alone.

keyTerms.meaning: That do not have with them, meaning no extra word comes along

phrases.english: We learn “ימים” that has no “months” with it
from “ימים” that has no “months” with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ זֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמּוֹ חֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: and let this one, which has “months” with it, not prove anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 using the same reasoning as step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ימים in 'עד חדש ימים' could teach that ימים means thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ימים comes with 'month,' so it cannot be compared to a ימים that stands alone.

steps.title: Maybe learn from the daughter of יפתח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning ימים from the phrase מימים ימימה in the story of the daughter of יפתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not learn it from here: 'from days to days' (מימים ימימה)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third possible source. This פסוק uses the word ימים without any 'years' or 'months' attached to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two answers worked because those פסוקים had an extra word like 'years' or 'months.' This פסוק has no such word, so the earlier answer does not apply. That makes it a stronger challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time, four days each year
And so on, meaning the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: But say we should learn it from here: “From days to days,” and so on,
phrases.notes: שופטים 11:40. The women went to lament the daughter of יפתח four days each year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proposed source. It gets around the reasoning of steps 6 and 8 because no 'years' or 'months' word is attached.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice of בתי ערי חומה as the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here ימים appears with no extra time word, so it should be just as fit to serve as the source.

steps.title: ימים is learned from ימים, not from ימימה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a גזירה שוה needs the same word. ימימה is a different word from ימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn ימים from ימים, and we do not learn ימים from ימימה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the source from יפתח's daughter. The word there is not exactly ימים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By אבשלום and by בתי ערי חומה, the word is exactly ימים. The phrase in שופטים includes the different form ימימה, so the match is not exact enough for a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A different form of the word ימים

phrases.english: We learn “ימים” from “ימים,”
and we do not learn “ימים” from “ימימה.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 with a new reason: the form of the word is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the sources: the words do not match exactly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ימימה is close to ימים, it could serve as the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גזירה שוה here needs the identical word ימים, so ימימה does not qualify.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה can link words that are not the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 10. The school of רבי ישמעאל linked ושב and ובא, which are completely different words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference does it make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'and the כהן shall return' and 'and the כהן shall come.' This is returning and this is coming, and they are treated the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A גזירה שוה can be made between two different words, so ימים and ימימה should be close enough. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By נגעי בתים, the school of רבי ישמעאל compared שיבה (returning) and ביאה (coming) as if they were the same word. Those two words are much further apart than ימים and ימימה. So the reason given in step 10 seems too weak.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: And what difference does it make?
But didn’t the school of רבי ישמעאל teach:
“And the כהן shall return” and “And the כהן shall come,”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, about a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning and this is coming, and they are the same!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ, וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ימים cannot be learned from ימימה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even ושב and ובא can be linked in a גזירה שוה, then ימים and ימימה, which are much more alike, should surely be linkable.

steps.title: An identical word beats a similar word
steps.stepSummary: The rule from דבי רבי ישמעאל, that different words can be linked, only applies when there is no identical word available. Here we do have an identical word, so we learn from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only when there is no word that matches exactly. But when there is a word that matches exactly, we learn from the word that matches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. It explains why we may not learn from ימימה, even though דבי רבי ישמעאל linked ושב and ובא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רבי ישמעאל used a similar word only because there was nothing better. For ימים we have the exact same word (ימים in בתי ערי חומה), so we must use it. A merely similar word like ימימה cannot compete.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only… (limits an earlier rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a priority rule for גזירה שוה: an exact word match always comes before a similar-sounding word.

phrases.english: This applies only
phrases.notes: He means the method of דבי רבי ישמעאל from step 11, linking two different words.

phrases.english: where there is nothing identical to it,
but where there is something identical to it —
we learn from what is identical to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and defends step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule that was used to challenge step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since דבי רבי ישמעאל linked different words, ימימה could teach about ימים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different words are linked only when no identical word exists. Here an identical ימים exists, so it takes priority.

steps.title: A second reason: the timing of ימימה is unclear
steps.stepSummary: Another version gives a different reason for not using ימימה. We do not really know that it means every three months, so it cannot teach a fixed time period.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: How do we know it was once every three months? Maybe it was four times a year at uneven times, or maybe one visit after four months and then one visit after two months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason why the פסוק of בת יפתח cannot be used. This reason is not about the word at all; the problem is that the timing is unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn a time period from a פסוק, the period has to be clear. 'Four times a year' could mean every three months, but it could also mean uneven gaps, like four months and then two months. Since the פסוק does not give a fixed gap, it cannot teach how often אבשלום cut his hair.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge against step 12. It is a second, separate version of why ימימה is rejected.

phrases.english: Some say:
From where do we know
that it was once every three months?
phrases.notes: The women went to lament בת יפתח four times a year (שופטים 11:40), which might seem to mean every three months.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was four times a year (at any times),
(or alternatively)
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words and some leave them out.

phrases.english: after four months one time,
after two months one time!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מְנָא יָדְעִינַן דְּכֹל תְּלָתָא יַרְחִין חַד זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason than steps 10 and 12 for rejecting the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning ימים from מימים ימימה altogether
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק does not give a clear, fixed time gap, so it cannot define a time period.

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: אבשלום cut his hair every thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the opinion of רבי נהוראי that אבשלום cut his hair once every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says: He cut his hair once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes רבי נהוראי's view from the ברייתא (step 2) so it can explain his reason. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the view was that ימים means a year. רבי נהוראי gives a much shorter time, thirty days. The next step will explain his reason.

phrases.english: רבי נהוראי says:
He cut his hair once every thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלֵּחַ אַחַת לִשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ימים discussion and returns to רבי נהוראי's opinion from step 2 in order to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום cut his hair every thirty days.

steps.title: The reason: after thirty days hair becomes heavy
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי's reason is that כהנים cut their hair every thirty days because by then the hair is heavy. אבשלום also cut his because it was heavy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? With כהנים, the reason is that the hair becomes heavy. Here too, the hair becomes heavy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי נהוראי's reason and gives it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים cut their hair every thirty days because by then it has real weight. The פסוק says אבשלום cut his hair because it was heavy on him. So we use the same thirty-day measure for him.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Regarding כהנים, who cut every thirty days,
it is because there is heaviness,
here too there is heaviness.
phrases.notes: The פסוק says אבשלום cut his hair because it was heavy on him (שמואל ב 14:26).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? גַּבֵּי כֹהֲנִים מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא כּוֹבֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי נהוראי say thirty days?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thirty days is when hair becomes heavy, as with כהנים, and אבשלום cut his hair because it was heavy.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: he cut his hair every ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says אבשלום cut his hair every week, from one ערב שבת to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: He cut his hair from one ערב שבת to the next ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and quotes רבי יוסי's view from the ברייתא (step 2), that אבשלום cut his hair once a week. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the shortest time period so far. It means a weekly haircut, as was done before every שבת.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says:
He cut his hair from one ערב שבת to the next ערב שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלֵּחַ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוסי's opinion from step 2 so the גמרא can examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבשלום cut his hair every week, on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Then how was he different from his brothers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי. If אבשלום cut his hair every week, he was no different from his brothers, so in what way was he a נזיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between him and the rest of his brothers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבשלום was a נזיר, and a נזיר is supposed to grow his hair. If he cut it every ערב שבת, just like the other sons of the king did, his נזירות would mean nothing special. The question shows that רבי יוסי's view seems to erase the difference.

phrases.english: What difference is there between him
and the rest of his brothers!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion of רבי יוסי from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that אבשלום cut his hair every ערב שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A weekly haircut is what all the king's sons did, so it would leave nothing that marks אבשלום as a נזיר.

steps.title: A midweek festival shows the difference
steps.stepSummary: When a יום טוב falls in the middle of the week, his brothers cut their hair for it, but אבשלום did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is a יום טוב that falls in the middle of the week. His brothers would cut their hair for it, but he would not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 17 by showing a real difference between אבשלום and his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His brothers cut their hair before every שבת and before every יום טוב. אבשלום, according to רבי יוסי, cut only from one ערב שבת to the next. So a midweek יום טוב was a haircut he skipped, and that is a kind of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: In the middle of the week

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שבת means 'week', not the day of rest.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶמְצַע שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A festival that falls in the middle of the week,
phrases.notes: Here שַׁבָּת means the week, not שבת itself.

phrases.english: when his brothers cut their hair,
he does not cut his.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶמְצַע שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a case where his behavior was different from his brothers'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting every week would make אבשלום just like his brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: He skipped the haircut before a midweek יום טוב, while his brothers did not.

steps.title: A different answer: the time of day on Friday
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: his brothers cut their hair on Friday morning, but אבשלום waited until late Friday afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, the difference is about cutting hair on the morning of ערב שבת. His brothers cut theirs then, but he did not cut his until the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, both cut on ערב שבת, but at different times of day. Waiting until the evening let his hair grow a few more hours. That small holding back was his נזירות.

phrases.english: Alternatively: cutting hair from the morning
of the eve of the Sabbath,
his brothers cut their hair then,
but he did not cut his until the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא answered in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer based on the time of day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting every ערב שבת seems to be exactly what his brothers did.
steps.terutzMaskana: He cut later in the day than his brothers did.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, אבשלום's נזירות was small: either he skipped the midweek יום טוב haircut, or he cut later on ערב שבת than his brothers.

steps.title: What do the forty years refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the 'forty years' in the פסוק about אבשלום are counted from.
steps.simpleTranslation: These forty years, what are they about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question about the פסוק on אבשלום quoted earlier. It asks what the 'forty years' are counted from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'at the end of forty years' but does not say forty years from what. So the גמרא wants to know the starting point, and the next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they about? (what do they refer to?)

phrases.english: These forty years,
phrases.notes: This is from the פסוק about אבשלום: 'at the end of forty years' (שמואל ב 15:7).

phrases.english: what is their purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the אבשלום פסוק, after the haircut discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The starting point of the 'forty years' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Forty years from when the people asked for a king
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי, in the name of רבי יהושע, says the forty years are counted from when the Jews asked for a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נהוראי says in the name of רבי יהושע: it means at the end of forty years from when they asked for a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the starting point of the forty years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count does not start from אבשלום's birth or from דוד's reign. It starts from the time the people asked שמואל for a king. That fixes the forty years to a known event.

keyTerms.meaning: That they asked for themselves a king

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Nehorai says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: לְקֵץ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לָהֶן מֶלֶךְ.
phrases.english: At the end of forty years from when they asked for themselves a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The forty years are counted from when the Jews asked for a king.

steps.title: That year was שמואל's tenth year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the year the people asked for a king was the tenth year of שמואל's leadership.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the year they asked for a king was the tenth year of שמואל from רמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a detail to the answer. It tells us when the request for a king happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 counted from the request for a king. This ברייתא places that request in שמואל's tenth year as leader. Now the forty years can be fitted onto the timeline.

phrases.english: It was taught: That year
when they asked for themselves a king
was the tenth year of Samuel the Ramathite.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ לָהֶן מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a date to the event named in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The request for a king was in the tenth year of שמואל.

steps.title: An unstated נזירות lasts thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if someone becomes a נזיר without saying for how long, it lasts thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An unspecified נזירות is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the default length of a נזירות when no time was stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might say 'I am a נזיר' and stop there. The משנה sets a fixed default of thirty days for such a case. The גמרא will now look for the source of this number.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזירות with no stated length

steps.whyThisMatters: This thirty-day default is the basic rule for any נזיר who did not name a time period.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Unspecified naziriteship is thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the אגדה about אבשלום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזירות with no stated length lasts thirty days.

steps.title: Where do we learn the thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the thirty-day rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the משנה gets the number thirty. It is setting up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not clearly state a default length for נזירות. So the גמרא wants a פסוק behind the משנה's number.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters learned?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for a thirty-day default נזירות.

steps.title: The word יהיה equals thirty
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא learns it from the פסוק 'קדוש יהיה': the letters of יהיה add up to thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא said: the פסוק says 'קדוש יהיה' (he shall be holy), and in גימטריא the word יהיה adds up to thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא answers the question with a פסוק about the נזיר, using the number value of its letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the נזיר 'יהיה' (shall be) holy. Counting the letters, י=10, ה=5, י=10, ה=5, the total is thirty. So 'he shall be holy' hints at holiness for thirty days.
steps.whatToRemember: A סתם נזירות is thirty days, learned from the גימטריא of יהיה in 'קדוש יהיה'.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said: The verse states:
"He shall be holy"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:5

phrases.english: the numerical value of yihye is thirty.
phrases.notes: Add up the letters: י is 10, ה is 5, י is 10, ה is 5, which makes 30.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גימטריא of יהיה in 'קדוש יהיה' is thirty, which is the default length of נזירות.

steps.title: בר פדא counts the word נזיר in the תורה and gets twenty-nine
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא learns the length of an unspecified נזירות from the number of times נזיר and נזרו appear in the תורה: twenty-nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא said: It matches the number of times the words 'נזיר' and 'נזרו' are written in the תורה, which is thirty minus one (twenty-nine).
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא gives a different source for the length of a סתם נזירות. He counts the appearances of the word נזיר and its forms in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא used the number value of the letters in יהיה and got thirty. בר פדא instead counts how often the word appears in the נזיר section and gets twenty-nine. The two sources give different numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא who gives a second source
His נזירות, one of the forms of the word נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume בר פדא agrees with רב מתנא's thirty. His count gives twenty-nine, so these are two different numbers from two different sources.

phrases.english: Bar Padda said:
Corresponding to "nazir" and "his nezirus"
that are stated in the Torah,
thirty less one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source, with a different number, for the question answered by רב מתנא in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The count of the word נזיר and its forms in the תורה, twenty-nine times, sets the length of an unspecified נזירות.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב מתנא also learn from the word count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב מתנא doesn't use בר פדא's method of counting the word נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מתנא too should learn from the words 'נזיר' and 'נזרו'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מתנא: the count of נזיר words seems like a good source, so why didn't he use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of the words is right there in the תורה. If it can teach the length of נזירות, רב מתנא should accept it and reach twenty-nine, as בר פדא does. The challenge forces רב מתנא to explain why he ignores this count.

phrases.english: And Rav Mattana too,
let him learn from "nazir," "his nezirus"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses בר פדא's source to question רב מתנא's choice of source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנא's derivation from the גימטריא of יהיה (step 25)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word count is a valid source, רב מתנא should use it and reach twenty-nine days.

steps.title: The extra נזיר words are needed for other teachings
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא would answer that the forms of נזיר are needed for teachings, so they can't be counted: a נזיר may not drink יין מצוה, and one נזירות can take effect on top of another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: That word is needed for a teaching. 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain (יזיר)' forbids wine of a מצוה just like ordinary wine. 'When he shall clearly utter a vow, the vow of a נזיר, to abstain (להזיר)' teaches that נזירות can take effect on top of נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב מתנא. Some forms of the word נזיר are used to teach other laws, so they don't count toward the length of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting words only works if each word is free to be counted. Here, יזיר teaches that even יין מצוה is forbidden to a נזיר, and להזיר teaches that a second נזירות vow can take effect while the first is still in force. Since these words already have a job, רב מתנא does not use the count and learns from יהיה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from a word in the פסוק
A second נזירות takes effect on top of an existing one

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for an unspecified נזירות: רב מתנא counts the letters of יהיה (thirty), and בר פדא counts the word נזיר (twenty-nine). רב מתנא doesn't use the word count because some of those words are needed for other teachings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step also gives two practical laws for a נזיר: even יין מצוה is forbidden, and taking a second נזירות vow adds another period.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
That one is for an exposition:
phrases.notes: He means some of those forms of the word נזיר are needed to teach other laws.

phrases.english: "From wine and strong drink he shall abstain"
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ג

phrases.english: to forbid wine of a מצוה
just like optional wine,
"When he shall clearly utter a vow,
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:ב

phrases.english: the vow of a nazir, to abstain"
teaches that nezirus
takes effect upon nezirus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by showing the words are already used for other teachings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source word is needed for other teachings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every form of נזיר in the תורה can be counted to set the length of נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some forms (יזיר, להזיר) teach other laws, so רב מתנא does not count them and relies on יהיה instead.
